stem: A 2-day-old boy born at term has passed no meconium, and his abdomen is distended. On rectal examination the rectum is narrow, and a gush of liquid stool follows the examining finger. A contrast enema shows a narrow distal segment with a widened colon above it.
oneliner: 2-day-old M + no meconium + distended abdomen + narrow rectum, explosive stool after rectal exam + dilated proximal colon → which embryologic failure?
ask: Which embryologic failure best explains this condition?

options.A: Failure of midgut rotation around the superior mesenteric artery
options.C: Failure of neural crest cells to migrate into the distal colon
options.D: Failure of recanalization of the bowel lumen
options.E: Bifid ventral pancreatic bud encircling the duodenum

whyNot.A: **Malrotation** causes bilious vomiting and volvulus; here a **narrow rectum with explosive stool** points to the distal bowel wall
whyNot.B: Leaves a **Meckel diverticulum** or umbilical fistula, not a failure to pass meconium
whyNot.D: Causes **atresia or stenosis** with a blind segment, most often in the duodenum, so stool would not gush out
whyNot.E: **Annular pancreas** obstructs the duodenum with early vomiting, not a dilated colon above a narrow rectum

answer: Failure of neural crest migration into the distal colon (aganglionosis)
why: Delayed meconium, a narrow rectum and explosive stool after a rectal exam suggest **Hirschsprung disease**. **Neural crest cells** colonize the gut from top to bottom, and if they stop short the distal bowel lacks **myenteric and submucosal ganglion cells**, stays contracted and dilates the colon above it.

idea.rule: Neural crest cells must reach the distal colon to form enteric ganglia, and failure causes Hirschsprung disease.
also: RET mutations are the most common genetic cause
Rectal suction biopsy shows absent ganglion cells with thickened nerve trunks
The rectum is always involved and the aganglionic segment extends upward for a variable length

stem: In a developmental experiment, neural crest precursors in embryos are labelled and followed as they leave the bowel wall and colonize organs that develop from the primitive gut. Sections of several organs are then searched for labelled ganglion cells.
oneliner: Labelled neural crest cells traced out of the bowel wall into gut-derived organs → where do the labelled ganglia end up?
ask: Which organ is most likely to contain labelled enteric ganglion cells?

whyNot.B: Develops from **mesoderm in the dorsal mesogastrium**, not from the gut tube
whyNot.C: Forms from **intermediate mesoderm**, not from the gut tube
whyNot.D: Cortex is **mesoderm**, and the medulla gets its crest cells from **trunk neural crest**, not the bowel wall
whyNot.E: Arises from the **ureteric bud** of the mesonephric duct, not from the gut

why: **Enteric neurons** come from neural crest that migrates along the gut and into organs that bud from it. The **pancreas**, a foregut bud, contains enteric ganglia, whereas the **spleen, kidney, adrenal gland and ureter** do not arise from the gut tube.

idea.rule: Enteric ganglia colonize the gut and organs that bud from it, not mesodermal organs.
also: Vagal neural crest forms most enteric neurons
Sacral neural crest contributes to the distal colon
Failure to colonize the distal colon causes Hirschsprung disease
Enteric ganglia are also found in the walls of the gallbladder and bile ducts, which bud from the foregut
